findings.title: Mutable default argument in CouponBook.__init__
findings.detail: Using a list as a default value causes the same list instance to be shared across all CouponBook objects, leading to unexpected state leakage.
findings.recommendation: Change the signature to def __init__(self, codes=None): and inside set self.codes = list(codes) if codes is not None else []

findings.title: Division by zero in average_discount when no coupons are present
findings.detail: The method divides by len(self.codes) without checking for zero, raising ZeroDivisionError for an empty coupon book.
findings.recommendation: Return 0 or raise a custom exception when self.codes is empty; e.g., if not self.codes: return 0

findings.title: apply_best_coupon crashes on empty coupon list
findings.detail: max() raises ValueError when called with an empty sequence, so calling apply_best_coupon([], total) fails.
findings.recommendation: Check if codes is empty and return the original total (or raise a domain‑specific exception) before calling max

findings.title: No validation of coupon percent in add()
findings.detail: Negative or >100 percent values can be added, resulting in nonsensical discounts or price increases.
findings.recommendation: Validate that percent is between 0 and 100 (inclusive) and raise ValueError otherwise

suggested_tests.title: CouponBook instances do not share default codes list
suggested_tests.rationale: Detects the mutable default argument bug.

scenario.name: Separate CouponBook objects have independent code collections
steps: Given a new CouponBook instance cb1
And a new CouponBook instance cb2
When I add a coupon "SAVE10" with 10% to cb1

suggested_tests.pytest_skeleton:
def test_couponbook_default_list_is_not_shared():
    cb1 = CouponBook()
    cb2 = CouponBook()
    cb1.add('SAVE10', 10)
    assert cb2.codes == []
